attributes.label: Arable farmers on  Schouwen-Duiveland
attributes.interest: Enough fresh water when their crops need it, above all as they germinate, to lower their farms' risk or to raise production. Many want to invest in measures that hold fresh water, once the technique, its costs, its risks and its gain in yield are known for the island's conditions; while supply from outside and measures on the island are both still debated, they hold back.
attributes.influence: Decide what the island's farmland grows and how each field is drained, irrigated and supplied with water: in 2025, 200 farms registered on the island grew arable crops on 9,094 ha, of the 13,752 ha of farmland of its 240 farms. A measure in the subsoil can serve several neighbouring farms, which collect and tap its water together; the study of the island's farms explored measures for clusters of one to three. Score 5: they decide the adaptation itself.
attributes.affected: Their farms depend wholly on rain and on the fresh groundwater under the dunes, the creek ridges and the thin rainwater lenses of the low polders: the island has no link to the main freshwater system, so in dry periods no water can be brought in and no ditches flushed, its shallow groundwater and ditches carry much salt, and the farms run short of water; drought in the growing season, subsidence and sea level rise make this worse, and the dry years 2018–2020 showed the farms vulnerable. Delphy's report on the island's freshwater demand (2023) finds farming on the island impossible without more fresh water; in 2026 a potato grower at Nieuwerkerk lost a fifth of his harvest to drought, had stopped growing onions for want of fresh water, and found ditch water at times nearly as salt as the Oosterschelde. Adapting is uncertain for them: the measures that store fresh water in the subsoil are not yet fitted to the island's conditions, their costs, risks and gain in yield unknown, so many farmers find the investment too risky to make alone.

attributes.label: Waterschap  Scheldestromen
attributes.interest: Safe dikes and dunes first; then an optimal use of the water system, its ditch levels matched to soil and land use, fresh water kept available where it can and fresh groundwater kept in stock, within costs society accepts. It has no task as a supplier of fresh water: measures beyond its regular water management are for the users of the fresh water to pay.
attributes.influence: Sets the island's ditch levels in its water level plans (peilbesluiten: Duiveland 2021, Schouwen 2022), matched as far as it can to soil type and land use such as farming, after a process with the people of the area; sets and enforces the rules for farms' groundwater extraction for irrigation in its waterschapsverordening, a notification within limits per hectare and per well, a permit beyond them. Score 5: it decides binding rules for the island's farms.
attributes.affected: Salinisation and drought enter its tasks: with sea level rise, drought and subsidence, more of its area faces salinisation; drought strengthens saline seepage, which is hard to undo; and drought, warming and salinisation affect the ecology of its waters. Dry springs and summers showed farming's need for fresh water in those seasons: supplying it is no legal duty of the board, yet a clear need in society, which it answers within its core tasks, using its surface water system to counter drought and keep fresh water available, exploring its treatment plants' effluent as a source and the sustainable use of fresh groundwater. Its budget for fresh water is limited, the costs fall to whoever benefits, and its legal means to charge them are limited. Farms' groundwater extraction asks more of its knowledge, monitoring, permits and enforcement, since extracting too much too fast draws up the salt water under the lenses; where too little fresh water is available, drying damages roads, nature and dikes.

attributes.label: Gemeente  Schouwen-Duiveland
attributes.interest: A vital and liveable countryside, with farming, one of the island's main economic pillars, made climate-proof against salinisation, subsidence and extreme weather, and a reliable water system; water basins on farmland fitted into the landscape.
attributes.influence: Its council sets the omgevingsplan, since 1 January 2024 the one plan for the use of all land and buildings on the island, farmland included; its executive decides where a farm may build a water basin outside its building plot; it pays part of farms' advice, research and machines for fresh water and climate-proof farming, and leads the Living Lab Schouwen-Duiveland. Score 5: it decides binding plans for the island's farms.
attributes.affected: Salinisation, subsidence and extreme weather put pressure on farming, one of the island's main economic pillars, and with it on the vital and liveable countryside the municipality seeks to keep. It budgets €1.1 million for a new Living Lab programme (2025), so that the farm sector stays diverse and resilient; its subsidy for farms' advice, research and machines for fresh water opens on 1 October 2026. The water basins farms build against drought damage have a spatial impact on the landscape, so the municipality sets how a basin outside a building plot is fitted into it.

attributes.label: Provincie Zeeland
attributes.interest: Keeping agriculture in the delta, for the fertile deltas' part in world food production, and strengthening nature; enough fresh water and good water quality, worked out with stakeholders in the Zeeuws Deltaplan Zoet Water; groundwater extraction in balance with its recharge.
attributes.influence: Sets regional water policy and the omgevingsverordening, whose rules reach the water board, the municipalities, residents and businesses, among them instruction rules the water board's water level plans and the municipality's omgevingsplan follow; sets the water board's tasks and rules of organisation and supervises it; grants the permits for groundwater extraction above 150,000 m³ a year, for drinking water and for open soil energy systems. Score 5: it decides binding rules for the island's farms, mostly through the water board's and the municipality's decisions.
attributes.affected: Zeeland has very little supply of fresh water of its own and salinisation as a specific concern; climate change raises the chance that demand for fresh water outruns supply, with negative consequences for agricultural yields and nature values, against its aim of keeping agriculture in the delta. Long drought causes water shortages, and sea level rise more (saline) seepage. Farms' groundwater extraction bears on its policy of balance between extraction and recharge: it researches registering extractions and extends the groundwater monitoring network to follow the small fresh groundwater stocks better.

attributes.label: Banks lending to the  island's farmers
attributes.interest: Loans a farm can repay from its cash flow, with its land and other assets as security; an investment whose returns are not yet proven they often count as a risk. In Rabobank's words, to be a partner of the entrepreneur and help farmers invest in sustainability.
attributes.influence: Supply 90% of the borrowed capital of Dutch farms (2018), Rabobank about 85% of the lending to the Dutch food and agri sector (2021); they decide whether a farm gets a loan and at what rate, judging more and more by its cash flow and the entrepreneur, as the Basel capital rules steer them towards profitability and liquidity, with land still an important security, and they count sustainability in classifying a borrower. Measured nationally: no source shows the banks' shares on the island. Score 4: they decide credit many of the island's farms depend on, without binding them.
attributes.affected: Among their farm clients, those in Zeeland face the greatest task with drought of the Netherlands' arable regions, in Rabobank's research (2023), above all because the province is relatively vulnerable to salinisation: the average arable farm's income has held up in dry years, higher prices outweighing lower yields, but farms with little access to fresh water or with salinisation problems can come under pressure, and less fresh water could force a switch to far costlier drip irrigation. Measured for the whole bank, Rabobank's provisions for expected credit losses carry an adjustment for the rising probability and intensity of droughts and floods, €87 million at the end of 2024 (€14 million a year earlier), its climate-sensitive sectors judged on five events, drought and water scarcity among them; no source read shows the banks' risk on the island.

attributes.label: Buyers and processors  of the island's crops
attributes.interest: Raw material of the volume and quality their plants and customers need. Cosun Beet Company, owned by its growers as a cooperative, wants the most value from the beet and good long-term returns for its members, its production in balance with its sales; a potato processor secures its supply through contracts that fix a volume and often its price.
attributes.influence: Decide what they take from the island's farms, at what price and to what quality. Cosun Beet Company, part of Royal Cosun, the growers' cooperative that also owns the potato processor Aviko, processes all sugar beet grown in the Netherlands: it sets how much beet each member may deliver (for 2026 cut from 100% to 90% of the allocation, after high yields and with sales limited) and advises its growers field by field. The Dutch potato processing industry turns about 4 million tonnes of potatoes a year into frozen products, an estimated 80% of them exported; of the potatoes for the industry, 5 to 10% are sold free and the rest under contract or in a pool (2020), a contract fixing a volume per hectare and often its price, with bonuses for quality and grading and deductions for tare; Aviko, Farm Frites, Lamb Weston/Meijer and McCain are the processors whose contract prices are reported. Measured nationally: no source read shows which buyers take the island's potatoes, onions and vegetables, or their shares there. Score 4: they decide the sales many of the island's farms depend on, without binding them.
attributes.affected: In a drought their supply shrinks and its quality falls, measured nationally: in 2018 the Dutch harvest was expected to be 23% smaller for potatoes, 13% for sugar beet and 44% for onions than a year earlier (CBS's estimate from a survey of 5,000 farmers), and north-western Europe's potato yield at least 15 to 25% below the long-term average. About 80% of the Dutch potato crop is sold to processors under contract, at around nine cents a kilo in 2018, while free-market potatoes reached 30 cents; many growers expected not to deliver their contracted volume, and growers asked the processors to share the cost of extra irrigation and to accept force majeure, while the processors held that a grower under contract should irrigate. Processors want potatoes of at least 40 mm, which many would not reach, and the potatoes' very high dry matter risked damage at harvest. No source read shows how salinisation on the island affects the buyers and processors.

attributes.label: ZLTO
attributes.interest: The continuity of farming and horticulture and a future for farmers and growers. On the island, more fresh water: in its island branch's words (2023), catching more rain and a collective system that brings fresh water to the island, a pipeline from the Haringvliet shared among the farmers.
attributes.influence: The association of 11,500 farmers and growers in Zeeland, Noord-Brabant and Zuid-Gelderland, in 44 local branches that speak for their members to the municipality and the water board; its board appoints the two members for unbuilt land, farmland included, of the water board's general board of 30; it takes the initiative in the plan that carries out the Deltaplan Agrarisch Waterbeheer in Zeeland, with the water board and the province; on the island its branch looks for more fresh water with the municipality and the province, and Delphy's report on the island's freshwater demand (2023), whose conclusions the branch welcomed, finds that farming there becomes impossible without more fresh water. Score 3: it shapes the water board's, the municipality's and the province's decisions directly by representing farmers, binding none.
attributes.affected: Its members' farms bear the losses: in a ZLTO board member's words (2022), drought salinised farmland, which harms crops, and made Zeeland's potato harvest considerably smaller; its island branch's chair (2023) expects the farms still active there in 2030 to have almost no income. It answers by asking for fresh water collectively: storage for rain, and pipelines from the rivers to farmland, which need large investments and more from the national government.

attributes.label: Consumers
attributes.interest: Food that is affordable, tastes good, is safe and of a known origin: across the EU, cost (54%), taste (51%), food safety and origin (both 46%) are the factors most often chosen when buying food; in the Netherlands nutrient content comes first (62%), and its impact on the environment and climate is chosen by 29%, among the highest shares in the EU (2022).
attributes.influence: What they buy reaches the island's farms through the buyers and processors: in the Netherlands about 4 million tonnes of potatoes a year become about 2 million tonnes of frozen products, an estimated 80% exported, sold through catering and fast food worldwide; when these closed in the Covid-19 crisis (2020), the market for processing potatoes collapsed mid-season, with about 1.5 million tonnes left in growers' stores. Dutch household consumption of table potatoes fell 15% from 2014 to 2017, to 13 kg a person, and Dutch production of table potatoes with it, to about 450,000 tonnes a year. Measured nationally. Score 2: they shape the farms' decisions indirectly, through the buyers' demand.
attributes.affected: In the 2018 drought, measured nationally, the potatoes and onions in the shops were smaller but stayed on the shelves. Onions became dearer, a kilo sometimes 25 cents more (LTO Nederland), as their trade rarely uses fixed-price contracts; potatoes, mostly grown under delivery contracts at prices agreed in advance, hardly did, though Albert Heijn saw both slightly dearer, supply being scarcer while demand stayed the same. The supermarkets' trade association expected consumers to notice little and not to eat less. No source read traces an effect on consumers to salinisation on the island.

attributes.label: EU
attributes.interest: Through its Common Agricultural Policy: farmers supported and agricultural productivity improved, for a stable supply of affordable food, a reasonable living for farmers, action on climate change and the sustainable management of natural resources, and living rural areas and landscapes. Through its banking rules: a resilient banking sector, financial stability and stable funding of the economy.
attributes.influence: Its Common Agricultural Policy is managed and funded at European level from the EU budget, through two funds: the EAGF, for direct support and market measures, and the EAFRD, for rural development, €387 billion for 2021–2027. Each EU country draws up a national CAP Strategic Plan from the toolbox of measures the Commission provides, and its payments are managed nationally, in the Netherlands by RVO at the tariffs LVVN's minister sets. To receive EU income support, farmers must respect conditionality: the statutory management requirements, EU rules on public, animal and plant health, animal welfare and the environment that bind every farmer, and the good agricultural and environmental conditions that bind those receiving CAP support; a farmer who violates them has the support reduced. EU funding for rural development co-funded the Living Lab's Samenwerken voor Zoet Water (2020–2022) and paid half of its drainage demonstrations on three of the island's farms (2022–2024). Its banking package (CRR III/CRD VI) puts the final elements of the Basel III standards of 2017 into EU law, the new Capital Requirements Regulation rules applying from 1 January 2025. Score 5: it decides binding rules for the island's farms, through conditionality.
attributes.affected: In the Commission's words (2025), water scarcity already affects 30% of Europe's land area every year, and will only worsen as the effects of climate change grow; it affects citizens, agriculture, the environment and businesses, with effects on health and on the supply of energy, food and drinking water, and leads more and more to economic losses across the EU. Its Water Resilience Strategy (2025) answers with, among other measures, a recommendation to improve water efficiency in the EU by at least 10% by 2030, each Member State setting its own targets, and a strengthened real-time early-warning and monitoring system for floods and droughts. Measured EU-wide: no source read shows how salinisation on the island affects the EU.

attributes.label: LVVN
attributes.interest: Sustainable, sufficient and safe food on everyone's plate, valuable nature and a vital countryside, for present and future generations. Agriculture, nature and food quality strengthen each other and sometimes chafe; it makes those dilemmas open to discussion and looks for ways forward together with others in society.
attributes.influence: Makes national policy, laws and rules for agriculture, fisheries, food and nature, whose compliance the NVWA supervises. Its minister sets the tariffs of the EU's Common Agricultural Policy support in the Netherlands, paid out by RVO to the farms that apply: for 2025, €174 per hectare of basic income support, €50.35 more on a farm's first 40 hectares, and an eco-scheme premium of €60, €100 or €200 per hectare for activities serving climate, soil and air, water, landscape and biodiversity, for a farm that keeps to the CAP's conditionalities. It publishes the Delta Programme with IenW and VRO, has directors on the Bestuurlijk Platform Zoetwater that advises the minister of IenW on the Delta Programme for Fresh Water, and with IenW, Rijkswaterstaat and STOWA had a knowledge programme on salt in agriculture, nature and water management drawn up (2025, €400,000 that year), on the salt tolerance of crops among its questions, carried out with Deltares and KWR among others. attributes.label: IenW
attributes.interest: A reachable country with strong dikes, where people stay safe and get from A to B, with clean air, soil and water, its living environment cared for and raw materials used sparingly. For fresh water, the goal it set with the regional governments in 2019: in 2050 the Netherlands is resilient against freshwater shortage.
attributes.influence: Responsible for national water policy, the safety, quality and availability of water among it, and for the working of Dutch water management as a whole; manages the main water system, the large rivers, lakes and seas, with Rijkswaterstaat carrying it out; may instruct provinces and water boards on regional water management where international obligations or interests beyond a region require it. Its freshwater policy ranks the uses of water in a shortage by the verdringingsreeks, which every water manager follows: agriculture in the last of its four categories, temporary irrigation of capital-intensive crops one higher. Its minister coordinates the Delta Programme for Fresh Water, which the six freshwater regions carry out, and manages the Delta Fund, which pays all of Rijkswaterstaat's freshwater measures in the main water system and 25% of a region's (up to 50% for innovative ones or those of several regions): just over €58 million for fresh water in 2026; early in 2027 the Rijk and the regions set the measures for 2028–2033. The Delta Programme 2027, which its minister presents to parliament with the Delta Fund's budget, proposes for the south-west delta that the areas with no supply from outside speed up their way to self-sufficiency, with no extra demand on the Hollandsch Diep and Haringvliet. Score 2: it shapes the island's adaptation through the province, the water board and Rijkswaterstaat; no source read shows the Delta Fund paying for a measure on the island.
attributes.affected: Drought brings freshwater shortages its policy must answer, measured nationally: in the Algemene Rekenkamer's report (2026), the 2018 drought did €450 million to €2.08 billion of economic damage in the Netherlands (Ecorys, 2019), and in the KNMI's scenarios an extremely dry summer of today is an average summer by 2050. The Rekenkamer finds that the Delta Programme for Fresh Water, which IenW's minister coordinates, has no concrete, measurable goal, so whether it is on schedule for 2050 cannot be judged; nearly three quarters of the measures studied ran 2.4 to 3 years late, and the first phase's spending, €512.5 million, came 40% above the €364.7 million estimated; while measures are delayed, the damage of drought persists. In the cabinet's reaction to the Delta Programme 2027, the Netherlands had a considerable water shortage in the summer of 2026, raised on 16 July to drought level 2, an actual water shortage: no social disruption, but damage and hindrance, with several functions and interests under pressure. No source read shows how salinisation on the island affects IenW.

attributes.label: Rijkswaterstaat
attributes.interest: A safe, liveable and reachable Netherlands, worked on together with others; in drought, the little fresh water of the large rivers and lakes divided as well as it can among all who use it.
attributes.influence: Manages the main water system for IenW, the large rivers, lakes and seas, the Delta waters outside the island's dikes among them, for national safety and fresh water supply. In drought it judges, as the water board does for its waters, whether water runs short, and divides the fresh water of the Rhine and Meuse through weirs, pumping stations and sluices by the verdringingsreeks. Most of Zeeland lies outside the area it can supply, where users depend on rain and groundwater; the island has no fresh water supplied from outside (the municipality, 2023). A pipeline to the island, which the province had explored (2021), would draw on waters it manages: the Volkerak-Zoommeer, at the Noorder Krammer or the Schelde-Rijnkanaal, or the Haringvliet, the study's most future-proof source. With LVVN, IenW and STOWA it had a knowledge programme on salt in agriculture, nature and water management drawn up (2025). Score 2: it shapes the island's adaptation indirectly, through what a supply route could draw on; none exists.
attributes.affected: Drought and salinisation fall on the main water system it manages: the fresh flow of its rivers keeps sea water from pressing too far into the country, and as the summer precipitation deficit grows, the possibility of supplying fresh water through the large rivers shrinks (IPLO, 2025). The Algemene Rekenkamer (2026) expects lower river discharges, above all in summer, more and more often, so shipping suffers drought damage more often, and a growing demand for extra flushing against salinisation; at low water levels ships sail with less load, cargo is spread over more ships and waits at the locks grow longer. When less water is available than is needed, it must divide the little fresh water there is by the verdringingsreeks. The Rekenkamer recommends that IenW's minister commission it explicitly as the executor of the Delta Programme's measures in the main water system. No source read shows how salinisation on the island affects Rijkswaterstaat, which supplies no water there.

attributes.label: Delta Climate Center
attributes.interest: Regional transitions towards sustainable, climate-resilient and prosperous deltas, in Zeeland and worldwide, with Zeeland as its living lab.
attributes.influence: A partnership of six knowledge institutes, Scalda, HZ University of Applied Sciences, University College Roosevelt, NIOZ, Utrecht University and Wageningen University & Research, at the Kenniswerf in Vlissingen, which started in mid-2023 with a budget of €88 million from the national government and the province, part of the national compensation package Wind in de Zeilen. Its themes for the Zeeland delta are sustainable food, water safety and water availability, and circularity, with three iconic projects from 2024: Delta Protein, the protein transition, mainly marine; Flexible Deltas, flood-defence landscapes that also offer a future for agriculture, salinisation and freshwater availability among their challenges, with living labs on the Westerschelde, the Oosterschelde (from the second half of 2025) and the coastal zone; and ProceZ. Score 1: no source read shows it working on Schouwen-Duiveland or with the island's farmers.
attributes.affected: In its own words, sea level rise, salinisation and drought are among the consequences of climate change noticeable in delta areas such as Zeeland, and it develops knowledge and innovations to keep them safe and flourishing. In its project Flexible Deltas, salinisation and freshwater availability are among the challenges of the polders behind the dikes, beside water safety, ecological functions and economic interests, which call for an integrated approach. Measured for Zeeland and the Southwest Delta: no source read shows how salinisation on the island, or its farms' adaptation, affects the DCC.

attributes.label: Deltares
attributes.interest: Applied research on water and the subsurface, for future, sustainable and safe deltas and a resilient infrastructure.
attributes.influence: An independent knowledge institute for applied research on water and the subsurface, working with governments, companies, knowledge institutions, universities and NGOs in the Netherlands and abroad. On the island it carried out, with KWR, Acacia Water, Agrarisch Schouwen-Duiveland and the municipality, the Living Lab's project Samenwerken voor Zoet Water (2020–2022), paid by the EU's rural development fund, the province and the municipality, whose quickscans gave 13 farmers advice on storing fresh water in the subsoil that fits the farm's soil, groundwater and economics, followed by five feasibility studies for groups of farms; drainage and infiltration, it concludes, can store far more fresh water underground than was thought; it wrote the project's final report for the municipality with KWR, Acacia Water and Buro Waterfront. With Acacia Water, Delphy, the trial farm Rusthoeve and the municipality it had anti-salinisation and double drainage on the low-lying poelgronden of three farms, at Kerkwerve and Dreischor, demonstrated and monitored (drains laid in 2022, closing meeting in 2024), half paid by the EU; with KWR and WUR it carried out LN2050, research on a climate- and water-robust layout of the countryside towards 2050, the island one of its three example areas, for its farmers, ZLTO's island branch and the Zeeland governments, part of the Ministry of Economic Affairs' Knowledge and Innovation Agenda; in 2025 it was among the knowledge institutes carrying out the national knowledge programme on salt. Score 3: the project's advice reached the participating farms directly; no source read says which partner wrote which advice.
attributes.affected: Salinisation raises knowledge questions it is among those answering: in 2025 it was among the knowledge institutes carrying out the national programme on dealing with salt in agriculture, nature and water management, which LVVN, IenW, Rijkswaterstaat and STOWA had drawn up because the growing salinisation of water and soil, partly through climate change, raises such questions, to fill fundamental gaps in knowledge, how salty the soil moisture becomes and how salt-tolerant crops are under Dutch conditions, and to make the answers usable in practice in models and tools; €400,000 was available for 2025, and the partners intend to find about €1 million a year for the whole multi-year programme (IPLO, 2025). On the island, the report it wrote with KWR and Acacia Water (Kaandorp et al., 2022) finds the farms' hesitation to invest working both ways: as long as the measures' costs, risks and gain in yield stay uncertain, farmers do not invest, and as long as they do not invest, the techniques are not refined, nothing is learned from building them, their effects cannot be monitored, and no knowledge base forms at agricultural advisory firms and contractors with which the cost of advice and building could fall; it recommends pilots with monitoring, and more research on the measures' economic feasibility. Following the report, it took part in drainage demonstrations on three of the island's farms (2022–2024). The EU paid half of their cost and the province and the municipality a large part, beside an own contribution from the participating knowledge parties.
